why_trail.why: The gate is a delete-not-repoint job: every playbook read/adjudicate/ripeness instruction retires outright, and the episode store only ever gains WRITE mentions. Two shipped compact-JSON spines are fully CRLF (135/135 and 66/66), so edits must be raw-text and newline-preserving. Both apply_episode_delta.store_root() and verify_episode_captured.main() carry an explicit comment naming g3 as the place that must pass --store-root explicitly, which resolves the handoff's own #308-shaped hazard.

Both c1s retargeted in place onto verify_episode_captured.py with an explicit --store-root episodes (the writer and the gate each carry a code comment naming g3 as the place that must pass it; without it an installed copy resolves the store under ~/.claude/skills/ and the gate exits 2 on every run). feedback.c2 deleted as terminal. One extra edit beyond the handoff: the archive imperative's 'leaving the unified AGENT_FEEDBACK.md at the agent-work root' clause was trimmed because it contradicted the archive.c1 I had just retargeted; the work-area move itself is untouched.

The auditor dispatch and its whole disposition-routing paragraph are DELETED, not repointed: the closeout now writes episodes and stops. Numbering 1-5 is preserved with episode capture as step 1 (the auditor that was step 1 is gone) and the surgical-JSON-edit rule kept as step 2; steps 3/4/5 and the lease release are byte-identical.

replacement-absent is GONE (4 -> 0). The last one to fall needed a real fix, not a bundle edit: verify_retirement._spine_names_replacement reads task IMPERATIVES, not check commands, so naming the capture gate only in admiral closeout.c2 left it 'wired but unspoken'. The admiral imperative now tells the agent to run the gate, matching the commander's. query_episodes.py is deliberately unbundled with a comment saying the omission is a default and naming the four routes around it.

The general test walks BOTH condition lists of both installed spines, pulls every *.py token out of each kind:'command' check, and asserts the skill installs it — plus a checked>0 assertion so an empty walk cannot read as a pass. The red proof landed on a PRECONDITION (execute.p2), which is the half a postconditions-only walk would have missed. apply_episode_delta.py is named only in an imperative, so no command check can see it; a per-name pin covers that half explicitly.

unapproved-store-mention 9 -> 19 -> 0. The 19 sites were re-derived through the guard's OWN store_mention_sites/normalize, never retyped, so an approval cannot be written in a form the guard would not recognize. Four reasons, all write-side: capture gate (ids and counts, never statements), install bundle, the bundle's default-not-a-boundary note, and the two spine imperatives. GAP FOUND, not mine to fix: the handoff's SS4 asks me to approve archive.c4's deny_globs entries too, but the guard has NO approval census for the retired-name leg -- only unapproved-store-mention has one -- so after g4 untracks the files those two deny_globs entries stay permanently red and test_canon_is_clean can never XPASS. scripts/verify_retirement.py is outside my allowed scope.

Full suite green with colour off: 1716 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed. Baseline at dbf9a23 was 1715 passed / 0 failed, so the only delta is +1 -- the new general spine-command test. Three existing install assertions were deliberately changed and each is named in the result; no other test file needed touching, which is the evidence that the bundle edit did not reach past its own callers. Blockers: none. One escalation: the handoff asks me to approve two deny_globs entries on a guard leg that has no approval census, so retired-name can never reach zero and test_canon_is_clean cannot XPASS -- verify_retirement.py is outside my scope.
